GROWTH VISION & ACTION PLAN

One Cohesive
National Strategy

As Head of Growth I will create one unified national team; all rowers rowing in the same direction: a clear agent profile, a recruiting playbook with a compelling value proposition, shared reporting a consistent cadence, and execution.

01 · DEFINE THE MANDATE

One strategy. Clear ownership.

Turn separate recruiting efforts into a national plan with accountable leadership and room for local expertise.

  • Define what the growth function owns, how it works with regional CEOs, COOs, recruiters, marketing, and brokerage leaders, and who makes each decision.
  • Establish shared priorities for quality recruiting, productive agent retention, recruiting economics, and the performance of the agent base.
  • Translate the strategy into a clear message: what is changing, why it matters, what each team owns, and what success looks like. Communicate it repeatedly and invite feedback.

02 · DEFINE THE RIGHT AGENT

The right agent, not every agent.

Build the recruiting profile around productive, durable relationships and Elliman’s luxury position.

  • Use production volume, transaction mix, market position, trajectory, client service, reputation, cultural fit, and contribution economics to define the profile. Set market-specific thresholds from real data.
  • Separate deliberate consolidation of underperforming agents from avoidable departures of top producers. Raw agent count alone is not the growth scorecard.
  • Create a target list of established agents and teams who fit the profile. Make prioritization and qualification consistent nationally.

03 · UNDERSTAND LOYALTY AND LOSS

Learn why the best agents stay.
Act on why they leave.

Listen directly to top producers and recently departed agents, then turn their experience into changes the business can deliver.

  • Interview existing top agents, newer successful recruits, and recent churns across regions. Ask what earns loyalty, what disappoints, and what would make the decision different.
  • Understand why agents choose Compass, The Agency, and other brokerages. Separate financial incentives from support, leadership, technology, marketing, relationships, and confidence in the brand.
  • Create a retention playbook with clear ownership, early risk signals, regular producer conversations, and follow-through on issues. Feed the findings back into recruiting and onboarding.

04 · SELL REAL VALUE

Make recruiting a business decision.
More than a financial negotiation.

Build conviction in what Elliman helps the right agent accomplish.

  • Translate the brand, people, support, marketing, market access, and technology into a credible value proposition backed by agent experience. Validate the claims before using them.
  • Lead discovery around the agent’s ambitions and business needs. Show how Elliman will help, then discuss economics in that context.
  • Equip recruiters with shared messaging, evidence, discovery questions, and a clear handoff into onboarding. Track whether the promises made become the experience delivered.
THE ARCHITECT & LEADER

Head of Growth

I architect, build, and lead the national growth organization. I own the strategy, team design, leadership, talent, operating cadence, and results, aligning recruiting and retention around net agent growth.

TIER 1 · DEVELOP THE PIPELINE

Business Development
Representatives

A national team of BDR peers, led by a dedicated role manager

Research and engage qualified agents and teams. Make calls, build relationships, and create well-qualified meetings for their paired growth executive.

Focus: Target quality, qualified meetings, and pipeline contribution.

TIER 2 · OWN THE RECRUITING CYCLE

Agent Growth
Executives

A national team of growth executive peers, led by a dedicated role manager

Prospect alongside a paired BDR, lead discovery and in-person meetings, and own the recruiting cycle for established agents and mid-sized teams.

Focus: Conversion, production added, economics, and successful integration.

TIER 3 · WIN STRATEGIC RELATIONSHIPS

Strategic Growth
Executives

A national team of strategic peers, led by a dedicated role manager

Focus on high-impact producers and major teams. Build senior relationships, mentor Agent Growth Executives, and coordinate their regional pod.

Focus: Strategic production added, durable relationships, and team development.

HOW THE ROLES WORK TOGETHER

A regional pod

Each market has a pod led locally by its Strategic Growth Executive. BDRs and Agent Growth Executives work together to build pipeline and win the right agents and teams.

Strategic Growth ExecutiveCoordinates locally · mentors growth executivesAgent Growth ExecutiveOwns discovery, meetings, and the recruiting cycleBusiness Development RepresentativePaired with the growth executive · builds qualified pipeline

Sales representatives belong to their national role team, rather than a geography-led sales hierarchy. National role managers own coaching, performance, and development. Regional pods own coordinated local execution. I build and lead the whole organization, partnering with regional brokerage leadership on relationships, integration, and retention.

BUILD THE NEXT GENERATION OF GROWTH LEADERS

A clear path to advance.

I will recruit primarily into Tier 1 and build a clear path to Tier 2 and Tier 3. Advancement will be earned through discovery skill, relationship judgment, pipeline execution, recruiting results, and the ability to coach others.

I have a broad network of talent at every tier. I will bring that network into the build while developing strong performers already inside Elliman and putting the right leaders in the right seats. Three tiers describe the work and career path, not a mandate for a large team. Start lean, use existing talent, combine responsibilities where sensible, and add headcount only when capacity and results justify it.

05 · BUILD NATIONAL VISIBILITY

Every leader knows the pipeline.
Every team knows the goals.

Create one view of growth, with consistent definitions and reporting across regions.

  • Define shared CRM stages, qualification criteria, required fields, owners, next steps, and expected close dates. Clean the active pipeline before relying on forecasts.
  • Track qualified pipeline, conversion, cycle time, production recruited, recruiting economics, onboarding progress, top-producer retention, and quality of agent losses. Show results by market, tier, and pod.
  • Cascade national goals into role, pod, and individual commitments. Review weekly pipeline and coaching, monthly performance and retention, and quarterly goals, talent, and strategy.

06 · LAUNCH AND IMPROVE

Build while the business keeps moving.

Start with a lean working system, learn from execution, and expand what proves useful.

  • Launch common pipeline reporting and priority producer conversations immediately. Pilot the profile, value proposition, and pod workflow with live opportunities during the first month.
  • Use Nemawashi to gather feedback and build consensus as the work progresses. Find champions across regions and give people clear communication, support, and expectations before judging their willingness to change.
  • Bring in the right leaders and targeted talent from my network, develop internal strengths, and address performance gaps with evidence. Make personnel decisions after expectations and support are clear.
  • Own adoption and outcomes. Adjust the structure, capacity, message, and process based on recruiting results, agent experience, and retained production.
